narratives.Description: Spec-path ingest harvests the accepted lean's Bound remedy items followed by its Acceptance Criteria items and writes one plan item, one clause and one pin entry per item, with a source record that names the issue, the cited lean and the harvest digest. verify:ac compares a Spec-path brief that is not yet on the merge base with that lean over REST, and a Spec-path brief that is only in the working tree with no source record fails and names the re-ingest command. Pain-audits record the harvest digest, a lean can give its items to slice issues through a Slices section, and the body route writes one clause per sentence-list entry.
narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer launching an ingested story, I want ingest to write the acceptance clauses for the accepted design (or for every body sentence) itself, so that I do not rebuild clauses by hand and an agent still cannot silently drop a requirement.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. markdown-scanners.ts: a level-2, position-aware, fence-aware Acceptance Criteria heading matcher and slicer for leans, a Slices section parser and the slice line parser.
2. New intake/spec-path-source.ts: the harvest (Bound remedy items then Acceptance Criteria items, or one slice label, or the unlabeled items), the source record read/write, slice ownership scan, and the live identity resolver used by verify:ac.
3. pain-audit-follow-through-gate.ts: harvest identity over both lists and the Slices section (unchanged digest for a lean with neither), the `harvest-digest:` carrier, and the count rule.
4. issue-ingest.ts: route order (slice line, then Spec-path arc, then body), one clause per harvested item with no task-statement derivation, the source record, slice refusals and the unclaimed-label notice, and one clause per sentence-list entry on the body route.
5. product-first-done-gate/evaluate.ts: the merge-base boundary that does not trust the HEAD fallback, the missing-record refusal that names `task issue:ingest -- <N>`, and the live compare against the cited lean, with a default REST reader of the source issue comments that tests can replace.
6. Contract text for the `harvest-digest:` envelope line, CHANGELOG with the one-time re-ingest cost, and tests for every Acceptance Criteria item.
narratives.Overview:
1. Harvest list. On a Spec-path ingest the harvest is the cited lean's Bound remedy list items followed by its Acceptance Criteria list items. The Acceptance Criteria heading on a lean is matched like the Bound remedy heading (level 2, position-aware, fence-aware). A lean with no Acceptance Criteria list is harvested as today, and an empty Bound remedy list still refuses.
2. One identity unit for a harvested brief: the list item title, read by the function `hashBoundRemedyBytes` uses, applied per item. The plan item, the clause text, the pin entry and the #3550 sentence list entry are that title. Ingest writes one clause per item in list order and skips task-statement derivation. The issue title and Description are not on the sentence list of a harvested brief. The body route keeps the sentence extractor.
3. Harvest identity covers both lists and the Slices section. The pain-audit envelope carries that digest, and the critic copies it onto its post as a `harvest-digest:` line. An audit counts for a lean only when its recorded digest equals the lean's current digest. An audit with no such line counts only for a lean that has no Acceptance Criteria list and no Slices section.
4. Source record and live compare. Ingest records the source issue, the cited lean id and the harvest digest on the brief. For a brief with that record, the `verify:ac` live compare resolves the lean through the completed-arc record of the source issue, harvests it over REST, and compares it with the pin. A recorded lean id that differs from the cited lean fails. A brief on the merge base keeps its merge-base pin, as today.
5. Earlier briefs. The boundary is the merge base. A Spec-path brief that is on the merge base keeps its merge-base pin and verifies as today, with or without a source record. A Spec-path brief that is only in the working tree and has no source record fails `verify:ac`, and the message names the one command that ingests it again. New ingests always write the record.
6. Slices. An accepted lean may carry a `## Slices` section that assigns each harvested item to one slice label. A slice issue body names its parent issue and its label in one closed line. Slice ingest requires the parent's completed-arc record, harvests the items of that label from the cited lean, checks the Target-digest against the parent body, and writes the source record with the label. The parent's own ingest harvests the items that have no label. Ingest refuses a label that another brief already records for the same parent and lean, and prints the labels that no brief records.
7. Body route. The whole-body pin, its extractor and its live compare do not change. After it builds the sentence list, ingest writes one clause per entry, same text, in order, including the title sentence and reference lines. No one-post criteria route is added.
8. Route order. A slice line selects item 6. Otherwise a completed-arc record with a Spec-path lean on the issue selects item 1. Otherwise the body route.
- Given an accepted Spec-path lean with a Bound remedy list and an Acceptance Criteria list, when the issue is ingested, then the plan items are the Bound remedy items followed by the Acceptance Criteria items.
- Given that brief, then each plan item has one clause with the same text and the ids are in list order.
- Given a list item that holds two sentences, when the issue is ingested, then that item is one plan item, one clause and one pin entry.
- Given that brief, when `task verify:ac` runs with no hand edit, then it reports no #3550 finding and no #5055 finding.
- Given a lean with a fenced example that contains an Acceptance Criteria heading, when the issue is ingested, then the fenced text is not harvested.
- Given a lean whose Acceptance Criteria list is edited after its pain-audit, when the issue is ingested, then ingest refuses because the audit no longer counts for that lean.
- Given a harvested brief that is not on the merge base, when its pin and Overview are edited together, then `task verify:ac` fails on the compare with the lean.
- Given a harvested brief whose recorded lean id is changed to another comment, when `task verify:ac` runs, then it fails.
- Given a Spec-path brief that is on the merge base and has no source record, when `task verify:ac` runs, then the result is the same as today.
- Given a Spec-path brief that is only in the working tree and has no source record, when `task verify:ac` runs, then it fails and names the ingest command.
- Given a harvested brief whose source record is deleted before the brief is on the merge base, when `task verify:ac` runs, then it fails.
- Given a lean with an Acceptance Criteria list whose only pain-audit records no digest, when the issue is ingested, then ingest refuses.
- Given an accepted lean with a Slices section and a slice issue that names the parent and a label, when the slice issue is ingested, then its plan items are the items of that label.
- Given that slice brief, then the slice issue body is not used as the requirement source.
- Given the parent issue of that lean, when it is ingested, then its plan items are the items that have no label.
- Given a label that another brief already records for the same parent and lean, when a second issue claims it, then ingest refuses and names the brief that holds it.
- Given a design with a label that no brief records, when any issue of that design is ingested, then ingest prints that label.
- Given an issue with no design arc, when it is ingested, then each entry of the sentence list has one clause with the same text.
- Given that body-route brief, when `task verify:ac` runs with no hand edit, then it reports no #3550 finding and no #5055 finding.
- Given a body-route brief, then its pin is the same as today.
narratives.Constraint:
- Harvesting only the Acceptance Criteria list (comment 6907835324 finding 1).
- A slice map in a separate comment (comments 6907893908 finding 1, 6907909549 finding 1, 6907962034 finding 1).
- A one-post criteria route with no critic (comments 6907777469 finding 2, 6907813363 finding 2, 6907835324 finding 4).
- A refusal for a lean with no Acceptance Criteria list.
- Making a Spec-path brief that is already on the merge base fail.
- Treating a missing source record as proof that a brief is old (audit comment 6908002468 finding 1).
- Counting an audit with no recorded digest for a lean that carries an Acceptance Criteria list or a Slices section (audit comment 6908002468 finding 2).
- An author or login filter on design comments. Agents post under the operator's login.
- Any change to what the body route admits.

Ingest currently turns background prose into obligations, creating unnecessary manual work. Automatically generating clauses is sensible, but the proposed narrowing does not preserve the stated protection against dropped requirements. ### 1. blocks-the-design — AC-only admission drops the restriction in the existing regression fixture

**Evidence:** At dispatch SHA `06eda7e1377a981bc80e34f218ba039a99c7247c`, `packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/sentence-floor.test.ts:683–718` places “Presentation changes only; do not change persistence or backend processing” **before** the Acceptance Criteria heading, then explicitly asserts that first ingest pins it. **Failure mode:** Under AC-only admission, the two positive checks become clauses while the restriction disappears from the protected set. An agent can subsequently remove that restriction from context without changing the admitted digest. This requires no sophisticated injection: ordinary section placement creates the omission. An untrusted author can exploit the same boundary deliberately.

There is also a concrete Scope example: `xbrief/completed/2026-11-15-6316-featscope-part-line-pre-merge-story-line-check-and-write-sto.xbrief.json:13` records Scope requirements for line-start/digits-only parsing and states that the part line is not a finalize-close signal; its AC list does not restate those requirements explicitly.

**Disposition:** The blanket declaration that Summary and Scope are context cannot bind while claiming unchanged requirement preservation. The strongest case for AC-only is that a deliberately complete AC section provides a simple, deterministic contract. That would change my verdict if completeness were an explicitly authorized source contract, or if protected restrictions outside AC remained covered. Hashing alone supplies neither. Retaining every reference sentence is unnecessary, but discarding every Scope sentence is not an equivalent remedy.

### 2. blocks-the-design — Narrowing admission alone leaves the independent sentence floor red

**Evidence:** At the same SHA, `packages/core/src/product-first-done-gate/acceptance.ts:337–398` collects sentence-floor text from the title, Overview, Description, other narratives, and item acceptance text. **Failure mode:** Keeping Summary and Scope in Overview as context while generating only AC clauses still produces unmapped sentence-floor findings. Conversely, silently narrowing both selectors removes the remaining check that could expose finding 1. These are two distinct checks, not one selector with two names.

**Disposition:** The design must explicitly reconcile the sentence-floor input with the admitted-source input. Automatic clauses alone cannot satisfy the promised “no #3550 or #5055 finding without hand edits.” This can reuse the existing checks; it does not justify adding another gate. Existing first-stamp lists also need an explicit compatibility decision rather than silent restamping.

**Failure mode:** Automatically attaching each sentence to an existing file inside `file_scope` can remove structural complaints while leaving the behavior entirely unverified. One sentence may also contain several obligations; one generated clause does not prove all of them.

**Disposition:** Clause generation can bind as intake automation, but its success must be described as requirement representation and launch preparation. ## Summary

Every story ingested for wave 2a (nine briefs, 2026-11-15) needed hand work before it could launch, and most of it was work the tooling could derive. The biggest single cost of the wave: about 170 acceptance clauses built by an operator script, plus two extra lifecycle PRs.

## What we saw

1. **Every ingested sentence becomes a required clause.** #5055 (admitted-source identity) and #3550 (sentence floor) together mean that every sentence `issue:ingest` admits, prose included ("Refs #6286.", "design-critique: not warranted ...", "Scope 1."), must be a clause with identical text and an artifact path. A confession does not satisfy #5055. The clauses for prose bind to CHANGELOG.md and read "unverifiable" forever.
2. **The sentence floor fails every fresh brief.** Ingest admits Summary/Scope sentences that it never turns into clauses, multi-sentence clauses do not map, and the first Acceptance Criteria bullet is glued to its heading.
3. **The launch fields are empty.** kind, UserStory, ImplementationPlan, items[].narrative.Acceptance, and the swarm block (readiness, parallel_safe, verify_commands, expected_outputs, depends_on, conflict_group, size, model_tier, Traces) all needed hand-filling before `swarm:launch`.
4. **Description is only the title**, which fails the story-quality two-sentence rule.
5. **Evaluator-surface record not in file_scope.** A story that touches a declared evaluator surface must renew `xbrief/evaluator-surface-disposition.json` in the same diff, but ingest never adds that path, so the worker is fenced out of it.
6. **Clause ids drift from items.** After a clause rewrite, items keep `clause.1..K` ids whose titles no longer match the clause text they key to. Completion keys evidence by id, so a wrong order puts evidence on the wrong requirement (caught by review on #6321).
7. **Green verify:ac before any work.** A clause bound to a file that already exists reads "unverifiable" and does not fail, so a brief can pass `verify:ac` before the work exists (#6316 on master).

## Expected

Fewer steps: an ingested brief is launch-ready without hand edits.

- Ingest admits only the Acceptance Criteria sentences (or the accepted lean Bound remedy) as requirements; Summary, Scope and reference lines are context, not admitted sentences.
- Ingest builds one clause per admitted sentence itself, ids in item order, each with a concrete artifact path from file_scope.
- Ingest (or promote) writes the derivable launch fields and asks only for the operator-owned ones (size, parallel_safe, model_tier).
- Ingest adds the evaluator-surface record to file_scope when file_scope touches a declared surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an issue with Summary, Scope and an Acceptance Criteria list, when it is ingested, then only the AC sentences are admitted and each becomes one clause with an artifact path inside file_scope.
- Given that brief, then `task verify:ac` reports no #3550 or #5055 finding without any hand edit.
- Given that brief with the operator-owned fields set, then `task swarm:readiness` reports no missing field.
- Given a file_scope that touches a declared evaluator surface, then the brief file_scope includes `xbrief/evaluator-surface-disposition.json`.

Refs #5055. Refs #3550. Refs #6321. Refs #6320. Refs #6286. Refs #6310.
